study type: Cross-sectional analysis of population-based survey data, assessing trends over multiple survey rounds.
cohort: Women in Karnataka, India, who delivered in the five years preceding each National Family Health Survey (NFHS) data collection round from NFHS-1 to NFHS-5.
finding: C-section rates in Karnataka significantly increased from 3% in NFHS-1 to 31.5% in NFHS-5, with higher rates observed in southern districts and private health facilities.
mod_finding: Higher maternal age, education, economic status, and delivery in private health facilities were significant determinants associated with increased odds of C-section, while women with pregnancy complications were less likely to have C-sections.
cross-section timing: Data was utilized from NFHS-1 to NFHS-5, with NFHS-5 focusing on women who delivered in the five years prior to the survey.
